## **Rules for Superposition**

### *10/23/2022, 10:37 AM*

I think I want to start writing down the rules for superposition that have been floating around in my head. Well, let’s begin\!

1. No contradictions allowed\!  
2. Something can only be real relative to an Ethus.  
3. Any Attribute of an Anti-Ethus will be in superposition relative to its Ethus.  
4. An Attribute may have an Anti-Ethus component and an Ethus component.  
5. If any part of a superposition breaks a rule, then the defining Attribute of that superposition joins its respective Ethus. 

That is, if my Ethus tells me that person G is at door 2, as a random example, then saying that person G is at door 1 is a contradiction, which breaks rule \#1. Thus, person G is at door 2, and cannot be in a superposition to also be at door 1\. However, if my Ethus tells me that person G is at either door 1 or door 2, then saying person G is at door 1 does not make a contradiction, and saying that person G is at door 2 does not make a contradiction, and thus, relative to my Ethus, person G is in a superposition between door 1 and door 2 of some specific proportion which may also be added to the picture.   
Now, if we know that person G has a 20% chance at being at door 2 in this example, then, by definition of it being a known, that is going to be part of our Ethus, and so that serves as an Ethus component of the Attribute of person G’s door-based position.   
Remember, by the way, that the Anti-Ethus is considered to be the set of all Attributes which are independent of the Ethus. That is, we could change any of these Anti-Ethus Attributes to whatever we want, and the Ethus will remain completely unaffected.   
So, for an example – when a particle goes through the double slit experiment, right, and it appears on the back wall, we can determine that if we do not know which slit the particle went through, then relative to our Ethus, the particle was in a superposition because of Rule \#3, and so it went through both slits at once. Then, on the back wall, it will be in a kind of wave function configuration, because of the logic of overlapping waves coming out of the slits and whatnot. That is, the likeliest spot for it to hit when coming out of both slits will be likelier for it to hit, and plotting this over every likelihood gets us the entire wave function.   
But then, if we turn on the sensor to detect which slit the particles go through, then if the particles were still forming the wave-like pattern on the back wall, and we checked the senser’s data, we would form a contradiction, because the wave would be implying that the particle went through both slits, and the sensor would be telling us explicitly which single individual slit the particle went through. Thus, if we saw the signature wave on the back wall still, and we would automatically break Rule \#1. So… we have to *not* see the wave on the back wall.   
But, then, we run into an interesting new query: what if we haven’t checked the sensor data yet??? We’re looking at the two non-wavelike blotches of particles on the wall behind the slits, but we still haven’t looked into the sensor data – all we know as part of our Ethus is that we set the sensor up and turned it on. And even if there was a power glitch or something that we weren’t aware of, and the particles would go right back to the wave pattern, so the point is that if we see them not in the wave pattern, then we can deduce that the sensor worked, even though we haven’t looked at its data yet. Maybe it takes us a minute to look at the sensor data, so… relative to the present, right, *before* we ever look at it, we’re going to still see the non-wavelike particle blotches, but the adding of the sensor to our Ethus still won’t happen until the *future*. So… are we communicating with the future??? I mean, if this were the case, it would not feel very fundamental / logically symmetric to me, so I want to find a simpler alternative to this question.   
My idea, then, is this: let us imagine a separate Ethus from ours, in which the act of us checking the sensor or not is part of the Anti-Ethus. Relative to this Ethus, then, because of Rule \#3, our checking of the sensor is in superposition, and so one “portion” of all possibilities involves us checking the sensor in the present. And because us seeing the wave pattern would break Rule \#1 relative to our Ethus, then relative to this other Ethus, Rule \#1 has already been broken in a portion of its superposition. Thus, because it is impossible to break a rule, we know that that rule-breaking-portion of that alternative Ethus must not exist, and so that particular Attribute joins our Ethus, (by Rule \#5):   
The person observing could possibly be in their own kind of wave function, because in one scenario, they look at the data right away, even if not in our “universe” scenario.

## **Severed-Ethus**

### *1/10/2023, 7:06 PM*

Ok, so – the Ethus is the abstract set of knowns something may hold on the world, and then the Anti-Ethus is the set of knowns which are statistically independent to the Ethus’s contents. Now, how about we add to the mix the “Severed-Ethus”, which is the set of knowns which are permanently in the Anti-Ethus. Specifically, though, this is a permanently not regarding the infinite nature of time, but instead regarding the infinite nature of possibilities. If in any possibility an Attribute may be added to the Ethus, then we know that that Attribute is not part of the Severed-Ethus. Because this “all possibilities” kind of talk is very similar to a superposition in and of itself, let’s define some Ethus-B which holds an Attribute in its Anti-Ethus such to create such a superposition. What would that look like? Well, maybe we just need to look at the central Ethus, which we’ll call Ethus-A. Any possibilities to answer our question or not will be located in the superposition-cloud of our very own Ethus-A. If such a cloud contains a possibility where Attribute-A, (the Attribute supposedly in the Severed-Ethus of Ethus-A) is in the Ethus, then Attribute-A is not in the Severed-Ethus, and so in order for there to be no superposition whatsoever, (or just totally compressed superposition), it must be the case that the Attribute “*Attribute-A’s placement in the Ethus or lack thereof*” must be in the Ethus. In other words, the Ethus must know that Attribute-A is not within it in order for it to be part of the Severed-Ethus – a fact which is kind of logically obvious if you think about it I guess.   
Ok so that’s probably not the groundbreaking aspect of the Severed-Ethus just yet. What is, I think, is that if something is in the Severed-Ethus, then in no superposition of the Ethus is it in the Ethus, (which, I would think, includes all time), and so it will constantly be in superposition. In the example of the double slit experiment, we can state that the slit of travel for the particles is forever unknowable if not measured due to Heisenburg’s uncertainty principle, and so therefore it is in the Severed-Ethus. Thus, even to the observer who Ethus-observes the situation after the fact, those particles, at the moment of the experiment in the past, are *still* in superposition. I think this hints at a bigger idea that I should explicitly state:  
The idea is that as an Ethus passes through time, its outlook on previous times may change. That is, something that is in superposition with respect to your current Ethus may not necessarily be in superposition with respect to your future Ethus, (in vice versa perhaps or perhaps not depending on the properties of Ethus addition which I do not yet know). So, even when describing the same Attribute/phenomenon, it may *change* its superposition state with respect to where *YOU* are in time. Get it? This is why the whole quantum world acts as a surprising misnomer – because it’s using all this same logic that *everything* obeys, but with some extra Severed-Ethus action in the mix because of the uncertainty principle. But any inherent difference is only an illusion.  
So, if we run my human version of the double slit experiment again with this stuff in mind, then here’s the breakdown of exactly what happens: the people move through the two doors while I’m blindfolded, and so relative to my blindfolded Ethus, they have most certainly gone through both doors at once, because the door property is in my blindfolded Anti-Ethus. As for what I would observe their pattern on the back wall to be in this state, it’s kind of, well, contradictory. Even the act of observing them will add their position to my Ethus, which will thus change my Ethus away from the blindfolded Ethus. And because I know that in such a scenario, it follows that their assigned door is not in my Severed-Ethus, it will thus automatically be added to my Ethus that they went through one and only one door, because if they were to go through both doors, a contradiction would fall into line somewhere in my superposition. Therefore, even imagining a scenario where I observe the result is linking to an imagined Ethus which has a non-wave function like scattering. All of this being said, at the moment, relative to my blindfolded Ethus, those participants still went through both doors at once, (assuming I didn’t have any other cues like sound or the like). (And yes, how this relates to the conscious/subconscious mind I’m not yet sure, so I’ll assume for now that the conscious mind’s Ethus is the default one in this case). But then, of course, after a moment I remove the blindfold, only to find that the people did *not* scatter like the double slit experiment’s quantum wave function – and that’s all thanks to the Severed-Ethus. 

## **Rephrasing the Three Laws of the Ethus**

### *2/8/2023, 4:42 PM*

I have been thinking about rephrasing the laws of the Ethus for about a week now, because there was a little bit of a blend between the old second law and third law’s descriptive information. Here’s what they used to look like:

| *Old Version* |
| ----- |
| Anything may only be real relative to an Ethus. Any attribute of an Anti-Ethus will be in superposition relative to its Ethus. An Ethus is invalid if a contradiction is triggered anywhere in the superposition of its parent Ethuses. |

And then to contrast that, here’s what I updated it to:

| New Version |
| ----- |
| Anything may only be real relative to an Ethus.  If an Ethus is valid, then any given property will be in superposition relative to it if and only if it is statistically independent to it.  Any child of an invalid Ethus will also be invalid.  |

To make it clear what/why I did this, it is because the new version makes for better laws, with each concept being “mutually exclusive” for lack of a better word from the last, whereas in the old version, this isn’t the case. That is, in the old version, we use the third law to access invalid parents based on the given Ethus working “backwards” in the tree – which makes for good practical application, but isn’t very law-like. Also, such a formulation doesn’t work to hint at the clear correlation between the contradiction and the clash of Anti-Ethus superposition, if that makes sense, which the new version fixes quite nicely. So, both problematic points are fixed there, and thus I like the new version better, as “laws” go.  
Another nice touch of the new second law, is that if you take its contrapositive, you get the following: “*If there exists a property which is in superposition relative to an Ethus, but is not independent to it, or is independent to it but is not in superposition, then such an Ethus is invalid.*” This is equally valid of course, by virtue of being the contrapositive, but I feel that it also has a nice touch to it all the while in the descriptive sense\! This is also precisely how we initiate the concept of invalid Ethuses, which the third law after that only runs with.   
Also, I should note that I like this new version because it pretty much divides the three-ish major discoveries here into just the right categorical laws. Pretty good, eh? In other words, each new law has something distinctly new to say that the previous ones did not paint the picture for quite yet.

By sharing their work on arXiv, researchers can receive feedback, establish priority, and gain visibility for their work. Here are some key features and considerations of arXiv: Submission: Anyone can submit a paper to arXiv, provided that it is within the scope of the site and meets certain formatting requirements. Submissions are moderated to ensure that they meet arXiv's standards for scientific quality and ethical conduct. Access: arXiv is free and open to the public. Anyone can read, download, and cite papers on arXiv without restriction. Peer-review: arXiv does not provide traditional peer-review, but submissions are screened by moderators to ensure that they meet certain standards for scientific quality and ethical conduct. Submissions may also be subject to post-publication moderation if issues are identified. Copyright: Authors retain copyright to their work on arXiv, and they are free to submit their work to traditional journals for peer-review and publication. Versioning: arXiv allows authors to update their papers after submission to correct errors or incorporate feedback. Each version of a paper is assigned a unique identifier, and previous versions are archived and accessible. Citations: Papers on arXiv are commonly cited in traditional journals and other publications, and arXiv itself tracks citations and other metrics for papers. Visibility: Papers on arXiv can attract significant attention from the scientific community and the public, especially if they address timely or controversial topics. However, papers on arXiv are not considered "published" in the traditional sense, and they may not carry the same weight or recognition as peer-reviewed publications. Overall, arXiv can be a valuable platform for sharing scientific research and establishing priority and ownership of ideas. However, it is important to note that arXiv is not a replacement for peer-reviewed publication, and papers on arXiv should be considered preliminary until they have undergone rigorous peer-review. |

## **How I Found the Aethus**

### *May 18, 2023, 10:52 AM*

I’m not yet sure how people are going to react to my Aethus idea, but for those who think it brilliant and intangible, there is something I should note:  
All I had to do was talk to the deepest layers of human intuition, and once there, these results came naturally. It wasn’t like I had to undergo some complex process which granted me magical concepts with no tie to accessibility — rather it is only when the deepest layers of accessibility are harnessed, does one find that they were known all along.   
This all being said, I want to hypothesize that, even if I have solved the measurement problem, I don’t believe that I am the first life form in history to solve the measurement problem, but rather the first life form to write a paper about it. All autistic people are surprisingly distinct, but I feel that there are certain breeds of low functioning autism that directly lead the individual to the solution of the measurement problem as base intuition. The problem is, none of these people can tell us about it, because as is a near unshakable law of psychology in my mind, language and Aethic discovery are directly combative. This is just my rephrasing of the Cognitive tradeoff hypothesis by Tetsuro Matsuzawa. That is, I argue that short term memory and the Aethic mindset were traded for language skills and a theory of mind during early human evolution. So the reason why I have the Aethic mindset, which in humans is normally only reserved for some low functioning autistic people, (who lack the language skills and the theory of mind out of having reverted to the old concepts), remains a mystery for now. I mean, in typing this I demonstrate language skills and a theory of mind, yet in hypothetically solving the measurement problem I demonstrate the Aethic mindset, however I can safely say that I have no kind of photographic memory like a chimpanzee or Temple Grandin might possess. Nonetheless, it seems that I have two otherwise universally incompatible traits, which can be argued for by the very fact that the measurement problem has not yet been solved and written about outside of me, at least as far as I can tell. Anyways, strange stuff\! 

## **Golden Biosphere Analogue to the Square Cube Law**

### *July 23, 2023, 1:42 PM*

Just thought of the craziest idea\! You know the quote about how advanced aliens might attack us like how boys throw stones at frogs? The implication I get from this is that such an alien biosphere is portrayed as just a scaled up version of our own so to speak in every aspect of society, such that we just get a biosphere which is far more advanced technologically, but interacts about itself in similar ways, such as they are precisely are to humans as humans are to ants.   
So, here’s why I think this won’t work:  
The idea is basically an analogue of the square cube law to Astrobiology, working in a similar way to how you can’t just scale an ant up to the size of an elephant. There has to be a transformation in the process instead.   
The idea, essentially, is that the capacity for us to destroy ourselves grows exponentially with technology, whereas the defense mechanisms put in place with our current society, given the tragedy of the commons and all, grows only linearly with technology. If we assigned each human comparatively limitless power, such that the advanced analogue of “boys” might attack humans with the same mindset as human boys attack frogs, then such an advanced civilization will implode as soon as it spawns. Why? Because the linear defense mechanisms of a human society would be immediately overtaken by the vast exponential issues propagated by such a technology.   
Anyways, so this demonstrates essentially two things: A) we will not remain constant in societal mindset with time, and B) we will be essentially forced through the keyhole of the Golden Point mindset long before we reach the capacity of supposedly treating humans like frogs to boys.
